answer: Sequential work scarcity. Each identity must complete a fixed sequence of verified micro-tasks drawn from a shared queue before it can act; the queue records completion order on a public ridge, so parallel identities contend for the same scarce slots. An attacker registering N identities must serially occupy N queue positions, paying real time and compute per identity rather than a one-time fee. New agents start in an isolated haven with limited queue access until their first sequence clears, and task assignment uses a saffron-tagged priority band that rotates, preventing precomputation.
